paper.title_en: Event-driven formulation of cosmic structure formation via Morse-Cerf theory
paper.abstract_en: Cosmic large-scale structure is described by evolving density fields, yet critical-point topology is usually analyzed through snapshots or threshold filtrations. We formulate the physical-time evolution of critical structures for a smooth, positive, coarse-grained density field using <math display="inline"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></math>. This monotone transformation preserves critical points, Morse indices, generic birth-death locations, and excursion-set topology. The resulting Morse-Cerf framework tracks critical-point worldlines, distinguishes Eulerian birth-death events, fixed-threshold events, and continuous level-set volume fluxes, and yields index-resolved balance laws and Kac-Rice intensities. As an analytically tractable proxy model, we use the Zel’dovich approximation while separating singularities of the Lagrangian map from Eulerian scalar-field bifurcations. The conditions <math display="inline"><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> define continuous collapse-crossing hypersurfaces, whereas local minima of <math display="inline"><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></math> define discrete nucleation proxies. For Gaussian initial conditions, we derive one-scale collapse fractions and crossing fluxes from the Doroshkevich distribution and characterize the proxy catalogs numerically at the adopted grid resolution. Their finite-time populations show temporally concentrated activity and ordered median growth factors, <math display="inline"><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">˜</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>nuc</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>fin</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo><</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">˜</mo></mover><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>nuc</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>fin</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo><</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">˜</mo></mover><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>nuc</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>fin</mi></mrow></msubsup></math>, over the reported smoothing scales, while their abundances and widths vary with smoothing. These discrete-catalog results are a fixed-resolution proof of concept, with no continuum-resolution claim. Continuous crossing fluxes and discrete proxy rates are complementary observables and provide a controlled basis for measuring exact Eulerian event processes in nonlinear simulations.
